problem_text:
Your teacher will give you some cards that describe events. Order the events from least likely to most likely.
After ordering the first set of cards, pause here so your teacher can review your work. Then, your teacher will give you a second set of cards.

Items to put in order:
- 10% of people are left handed. The chance that a randomly chosen person is left handed.
- The offspring of two fruit flies in a science experiment have a 75% chance of having redeyes. The chance that the first fly to hatch has red eyes.
- The weather report says there is a 20% chance of rain tomorrow. The chance of rain tomorrow.
- Half of the cards in a deck are red and half are black. Shuffle the cards and select the first card. The chance that the card is red.

This involves recognizing and using numerical representations of likelihoods, which aligns with the descriptor: 'Recognize, apply, create, or translate across multiple representations of fractions (e.g., visual models of equivalent fractions) and rational numbers (decimals, fractions, percents).' The student converts verbal probability statements into comparable numerical values.

This involves identifying a common structure—numerical probability values—and ordering them from least to most likely, which matches the descriptor: 'Identify patterns in numbers... and generalize them using words, pictures, or symbols.' The student generalizes that higher percentages correspond to higher likelihoods.

Using the practice definitions and descriptors, put these practices in the order in which a student working on this item uses them, from the first step to the last. Say what the student does at each step, and explain why the steps come in this order.
